title: Forget Snack Machines. This One Refills Itself
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: The guest gives first-hand operating details, then promotes his real estate business and social accounts at the end.

stated_problem.quote: So you're like, man, how do we turn this cost center into a profit center?
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: Ice and water vending
idea.one_liner: Self-service ice and water vending at high-traffic leased or revenue-share sites, earning money from each sale.
idea.customer: Passing consumers and work crews buying ice or water.
idea.offer: On-site vending of bagged ice and water.
idea.revenue_model: Per-item vending sales, with site rent or revenue share as costs.

acquisition_channels.details: Networks with local ice and water station owners.
Uses Facebook to meet owners and discuss deals.
Visits machines and calls listed owners to negotiate purchases.
Texts owners after visiting machines to discuss deals.
Everest, Cooler Ice, and Twice the Ice may help buyers find a location.
Relies on high-traffic roadside or car-wash locations for walk-up vending customers.

ideas.delivery: Self-service machines dispense ice and water and are monitored or reset through a phone app. The owner and a technician clean, collect cash and coins, clear jams, and handle physical repairs; sites are leased or revenue-share locations.

tools: phone app for machine monitoring and resets
prices: two to three times annual profit

ideas.other_uk_rules: The transcript describes Texas permitting. A UK rollout would need local siting/planning checks and compliance for ice sold for consumption, including food hygiene and potable-water requirements. Cold texts to individual or sole-trader owners used for deal sourcing would raise PECR concerns; cold calls should screen TPS/CTPS.
